raw_response:
Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple, bilateral, peripheral pulmonary nodules and opacities (indicated by arrows), some of which appear to have central lucency or cavitation. This pattern of multifocal, wedge-shaped, or rounded peripheral lesions is the classic radiological presentation of septic pulmonary emboli, typically arising from a source like right-sided endocarditis or an infected intravascular device. While cavitating metastases and granulomatosis with polyangiitis can present similarly, the distribution and morphology strongly favor an embolic infectious etiology.
